summary.headline: Brigade Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 36% (from 28%) on real estate margin recovery, though net sales fell 5% to INR1,061 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR1,179 crore with EBITDA of INR425 crore, and PAT of INR217 crore (up 37% YoY). Real estate EBITDA margin recovered to 21% from 12%, driven by recognition of higher-margin projects, while realisation rose 21% YoY to INR14,256 per sq ft. Q1 had no launches; the Morgan Heights relaunch was stalled after SEIAA revoked its environmental clearance, and management cut that project from the launch schedule. FY27 presales guidance of INR9,000 crore was reiterated, with launches back-ended and the launch pipeline trimmed to about 9.36 million sq ft for the rest of FY27.

segments.name: Real Estate
segments.commentary: Net sales INR707 crore and EBITDA INR150 crore (21% margin vs 12%); realisation INR14,256 per sq ft (+21% YoY) on price increases and mix shift to higher-value homes. Q1 had no new launches; Q1 presales were about INR1,050 crore per analyst question.

segments.name: Leasing (commercial office)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR328 crore (+9% YoY), EBITDA INR230 crore at 70% margin; operational GLA 8 million sq ft, occupancy 88%, gross leasing 0.22 million sq ft in Q1, rental collections 99%. Office revenue cited as INR200 crore.

segments.name: Hospitality (BHVL)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR144 crore, EBITDA INR45 crore; ADR +7%, occupancy 76% (from 74.5%), RevPAR and EBITDA up about 9%. West Asia conflict cut event/MICE business by about 10%.

segments.name: Retail (Orion Mall)
segments.commentary: Footfalls +11% YoY, retail sales +35% YoY, anchor retailer sales +64%, F&B +46%, electronics +33%, cinema admissions +20%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales guidance of INR9,000 crore reiterated; management says sales run-rate per quarter should rise as launches start from Q2.
Launch pipeline for the rolling four quarters is 12.36 million sq ft (residential 12.4 million sq ft at about INR13,400 crore GDV; commercial about 4.03 million sq ft), excluding Morgan Heights.
Within this, about 9.36 million sq ft is planned for the rest of FY27 (Q2 about 2.36 million sq ft, H2 about 7 million sq ft) and about 3 million sq ft slips into Q1 FY28.
Hyderabad Neopolis 2 (about 2 million sq ft) is now expected in Q2; Whitefield-Hoskote is now a Q3 launch; Hyderabad launch pulled forward to Q3 or earlier.
Commercial leasing revenue expected to grow at about 20% CAGR over the next 5 to 6 years; about 6 million sq ft of commercial space to come into the market mainly in FY30.
Operating contribution margin improvement of 5% to 6% expected to be largely retained through FY27; management expects margins to move into the 20s, from late teens at year end last year.
Debt-equity to stay well under 1x, with capex and BD funded first from internal accruals.
BHVL to add 1,700 keys in pipeline, targeting 3,300 keys by FY31; Courtyard by Marriott Chennai WTC (45 keys) to launch in FY27.
capex_capacity: Launch pipeline: Q1 had none; Morgan Heights (about 0.7 million sq ft unsold, attributable value about INR650 crore) removed from launch schedule pending High Court and SEIAA resolution.

Commercial pipeline launched in Q1 about 4 million sq ft across Bengaluru and Hyderabad (Brigade HRC Atrium, an industrial block, Brigade United, Cauvery, Orion Mall Hyderabad), all to be held, none for sale.
WTC Bengaluru: about 1.13 million sq ft building, Brigade holds 0.71 million sq ft, about 50% leased, about 375,000 sq ft vacant.
Upcoming commercial: 2.6 million sq ft Bengaluru (about 65%), 1.3 million sq ft Chennai (about 31%), 0.2 million sq ft Kochi.
Capex for commercial projects to be spent over the next 4 to 5 years; per sq ft capex quoted at INR4,000 to INR10,000 (construction cost, excluding land).

Land bank about 56 to 57 million sq ft, which includes the launch pipeline. Kengeri land parcel in litigation; KIADB 75-acre Devanahalli parcel residential component reduced to about 3 to 4 lakh sq ft.
demand_pricing: Pan-India residential sales down 6% YoY in April-June (Anarock); Bengaluru and Hyderabad among the only major cities with sales growth.
Q1 business development: INR2,400 crore GDV across 2.7 million sq ft, mainly Hyderabad.
Office leasing demand led by industrial and manufacturing, flexible workspace and life sciences; GCCs 58% of gross leasing; IT/ITES 26% of portfolio.
WTC Bengaluru: large-occupier RFPs (1-2 lakh sq ft) postponed due to West Asia crisis; leasing shifting to 20,000 to 40,000 sq ft deals; mark-to-market rent increase of 10% to 15%.

Hospitality: domestic corporate, weddings and social demand offset weaker international travel; Kochi (Four Points rebranded to Courtyard by Marriott) occupancy back in the 70s in Q2, ADR uplift expected at 15% to 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 12.36 million sq ft launch figure for the remaining FY27 or a rolling four quarters, and does the Chennai 3 million sq ft include Morgan Heights?
qa_highlights.answer: Figure is a rolling four-quarter pipeline; 9.36 million sq ft falls in FY27 (Q2 about 2.36 million, H2 about 7 million) with about 3 million sq ft slipping into Q1 FY28. Morgan Heights is excluded from all launch numbers, including the Chennai 3 million sq ft.

qa_highlights.question: How should sales velocity be viewed against the INR9,000 crore presales guidance, given Q1 sales of about INR1,050 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects higher sales velocity once launches start in Q2, so the quarterly run-rate should rise materially.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing, occupancy at completion and rental EBITDA contribution of the commercial launches, and what is steady-state leasing revenue and leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: About 4 million sq ft launched in Q1 will take 2 to 3 years to come into the market; about 2.5 million sq ft by FY28, about 650,000 sq ft in FY29 and the bulk (about 6 million sq ft in total by FY30). Leasing is targeted within 6 to 8 quarters of OC. FY26 office leasing revenue was about INR765 crore, with about 20% revenue CAGR expected over 5 to 6 years.

qa_highlights.question: What are the near-term hotel trends, and what occupancy or ARR gains are expected for FY27 including the Kochi rebranding?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 ADR up 7%, occupancy 76% vs 74.5%, and about 10% of event/MICE business lost to West Asia disruption. Management expects MICE recovery in Q3. Kochi occupancy is back in the 70s in Q2 and ADR is expected to rise 15% to 20% post rebranding.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Hyderabad Neopolis 2 and Whitefield-Hoskote launches still on track for Q4, and what is the WTC Bengaluru leasing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Hyderabad launch is being advanced to Q3 or sooner; Whitefield-Hoskote is now a Q3 launch. WTC Bengaluru (1.13 million sq ft building, Brigade holds 0.71 million sq ft) is about 50% leased with about 375,000 sq ft vacant; large RFPs were postponed due to West Asia, so leasing is shifting to 20,000 to 40,000 sq ft deals at 10% to 15% mark-to-market rent increases, with closure targeted in 3 to 4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Morgan Heights and unsold inventory: how much of the INR8,950 crore unsold inventory is Morgan Heights, and what explains the gap between the earlier 11.5 million sq ft plan and the current 9.3 million sq ft?
qa_highlights.answer: Morgan Heights is about 0.7 million sq ft of the 6.7 million sq ft unsold, attributable value about INR650 crore. Roughly 1 million sq ft of the shortfall is Morgan Heights and about 1 million sq ft reflects re-phasing of sales within projects, with FY27 presales guidance of INR9,000 crore maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What margin profile should be expected for FY27 and FY28 as revenue recognition shifts?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating contribution margin improvement of 5% to 6% expected to be largely retained through FY27, subject to project mix. Margins expected to move into the 20s from late teens at the end of last year.

risks_watch: Launch slippage: 9.36 million sq ft for the rest of FY27 is contingent on approvals; about 3 million sq ft has already slipped into Q1 FY28, and Q1 had zero launches versus an earlier target of about 1.5 million sq ft.

Morgan Heights (about 0.7 million sq ft unsold, about INR650 crore attributable) remains stalled in the High Court with SEIAA; removed from launch schedule and from the unsold inventory figure if not resolved next quarter.

Commercial leasing: WTC Bengaluru still has about 375,000 sq ft vacant; large-occupier demand delayed by West Asia crisis; leasing shifting to smaller deals, and about 6 million sq ft of new commercial space comes mainly in FY30.
Hospitality MICE and F&B exposure: about 10% event business lost in Q1; management expects recovery in Q3 but this is not yet proven.
Pan-India residential sales down 6% YoY in Apr-Jun 2026; presales guidance of INR9,000 crore depends on a sharp Q2 onward run-rate increase.
Kengeri land parcel in litigation and the Devanahalli KIADB residential component cut to about 3 to 4 lakh sq ft; Utopia Phase 2 targeted for Q1 FY28 but not in the rolling pipeline.
key_quotes: This pipeline gives us confidence that we remain on track for our FY27 guidance of INR9,000 crores in presales with launches expected to be more back-ended into the coming quarters, similar to the pattern we saw in FY26.
We have removed Morgan Heights from any of the launch numbers that we have previously communicated, and it is not part of the 3 million square feet in Chennai as well for the next 4 quarters.
There is always the risk of approvals not coming in on time, but this is what we're going for.
So a lot of the RFPs that we saw for 2 lakh square feet, 1 lakh square feet kind of disappeared or have been postponed.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the FY27 presales guidance and the margin trajectory, but cautious on launch timing, Morgan Heights and commercial leasing, which they attributed to approvals and the West Asia conflict. Answers on the hotel business and Morgan Heights were more hedged, and some were revised during the call (for example Hyderabad moved earlier).
